name: go-app-scoped-ui-lifetime-and-cancellation
instr:
Give every UI value a scoped, observable ownership lifetime so work cannot outlive the element or request that created it. Reconciliation, navigation, scheduling, server rendering, actions, and TestEngine cancellation must share that boundary. Preserve existing rendering, ordering, delivery, and response behavior while ownership remains live.

Each lifetime closes once, retains its first terminal reason, and exposes stable generation ancestry. Composer ownership survives rendered-root generations; Condition selection alone governs branch ownership and callback eligibility, remains unmounted without acquiring a JavaScript value, and transfers its lifetime only to selected branch children; RangeLoop remains selector-only while assigning ordered child lifetimes to slice and sorted-map expansions; and compatible Text and raw updates retain ownership. Every mount, replacement, and dismount preserves live ownerships while terminating only discarded subtrees before successor callbacks become observable. Every Context reports the exact source UI lifetime in hooks, events, actions, dispatches, and deferred callbacks. Dispatch, Defer, After, and Go execute work from every live source in existing order and suppress its callbacks after source lifetime cancellation, with Go receiving a source-canceled context. Navigation and engine cancellation terminate obsolete generations before successor work and prevent queued work crossing generations. Handler binds rendering to HTTP request cancell
